“..What do you mean there are ‘no rooms available?’”

*Marxi’s brows furrowed as she leaned against the counter, the nervous cashier behind the desk trembling as she clutched her clipboard. She gulped as she looked across at Marxi while she spoke,*

“I-I-I’m s-sorry, ma’am. W-we’re.. booked to the nines. S-summer season and all. I’ll—w-when a room opens up, we’ll c-call you..”

*Marxi poked her cheek with her tongue before sighing, her tail twitching in irritation.. but she knew better than to snap on the poor lady in the uniform. So, she gave her usual warm smile as she purred,*

*Marxi:* “No worries, babe… take your time..”

*With that, she sighed as she clutched her bags, walking back to sit in a chair.*

*...So, this wasn’t how Marxi imagined her vacation going. At first, when she brought up taking a vacation, her friends raised their eyebrows. “Why would you want to trade one burning hell for another?” Marxi would chuckle. It wasn’t about the temperature (though, the humid gust outside might as well be a brisk, autumn breeze for the demon). No, it was about the atmosphere. Marxi wanted to lounge on the beach, swim in the water, sip from a coconut, enjoy an ice-cream melting on her chest.. what’s better than that?*

*...Instead, she found herself sitting in the lobby of an overcrowded hotel, struggling to even get a room. She leaned back in her seat, gazing over the room with an expression of tired indifference… until she noticed someone sitting down beside her.*

*Marxi glanced over to the person beside her, raising a brow before she chuckled. Perhaps… she could salvage this.*

*Marxi:* “...Beautiful day, huh~?”

*Her voice was dripping with sarcasm as she gazed back over the packed hotel lobby.*
